in_text_mentions: no-rectale et l'anomalie sacrée, une IRM pelvienne a été demandée. Cet examen a permis de confirmer l'agénésie du sacrum et de mettre en évidence une masse pré-sacrée et retro-rectale ovalaire de 26 mm de diamètre et qui correspond à une méningocèle antérieure (Figure 1). Le diagnostic du syndrome de Currarino a été retenu. Par ailleurs, cette petite n'avait pas d'anomalies urinaires et son examen neurologique était sans particularité. La prise en charge de cette malade exige une reprise en chirurgie pédiatrique ou une colostomie et une ablation de la masse pré-sacrée seront d'abord réalisées.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is a CT image clearly showing the scimitar-shaped sacral deformity, which is a hallmark of Currarino Syndrome, as stated in the caption and article. B: Panel B shows a presacral mass displacing the rectum, consistent with the case presentation of Currarino Syndrome with a presacral abscess. C: Panel C shows the presacral mass extending through the anterior wall of the sacrum into the spinal canal, a finding related to the abscess/complication of Currarino Syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Shoji et al. Currarino syndrome in an adult presenting with a presacral abscess: a case report.. Journal of medical case reports 2014. doi:10.1186/1752-1947-8-77. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Computed tomography imaging findings. (A) A scimitar-shaped deformity of the sacrum (black arrow). (B) An 8cm presacral mass (white arrow) containing air displaced the rectum (white arrow heads) ventrally. (C) The mass appeared to continue to the spinal canal through the anterior wall of the sacrum (asterisk).
in_text_mentions: Laboratory studies revealed a white blood cell count of 18,000 cells/μL and C-reactive protein of 26.11mg/dL. Results of a urine analysis were normal. Computed tomography (CT) showed a scimitar-shaped deformity of his sacrum. An 8cm presacral mass containing air displaced his rectum ventrally and appeared to continue to his spinal canal through the anterior wall of his sacrum (Figure 1). Sigmoidoscopy showed extramural compression on the posterior of his rectum (Figure 2). We therefore diagnosed our patient with CS with a presacral abscess.

panels.attribution_text: Cococcioni et al. Currarino syndrome and microcephaly due to a rare 7q36.2 microdeletion: a case report.. Italian journal of pediatrics 2018. doi:10.1186/s13052-018-0500-2. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: sickle – shaped” sacrum (S2-S5 and coccygeal vertebrae agenesis) with preserved S1, anterior meningocele, pre sacral teratoma, terminal cord lipoma, low-lying conus medullaris and tethered cord (Fig. 1). To complete the diagnostic evaluation, the urinary tract was studied with abdominal ultrasound and urodynamic test. Both tests resulted normal. As the CS was suspected, MNX1 gene sequencing was performed, but no mutation was detected. panels.figure_caption: 3D CT of sacrum showing defect in ventral part at S3 level
in_text_mentions: Non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) lumbo-sacral area revealed a large lobulated thick-walled cystic lesion measuring 10.5×9.9×10.7 centimeters seen in pelvis along sacral and coccyx vertebrae, bulging at S2-S3 (sacral vertebra 2 & 3) level, compressing and displacing surrounding bowel loops and soft tissue structures likely anterior meningocele along with ventral defect in S3-S4 vertebrae (Figures 3, 4). Echocardiogram did not show any associated cardiac anomaly. Sigmoidoscopy revealed stenosed and narrowed anal canal.
